subject: chemistry-2
question: A laboratory solution measured at 25 °C has a pOH of 4.5. What is its pH, and how should the solution be classified?
explanation:
At 25 °C the ion product of water (Kw = 1 × 10^-14) gives pH + pOH = 14, so a pOH of 4.5 corresponds to a pH of 14 - 4.5 = 9.5. Because 9.5 is above 7, hydroxide exceeds hydronium and the solution is basic. Option D comes from adding rather than subtracting, option A from assuming pH equals pOH, and option C from misclassifying a pH above 7.

ELI-10: pH and pOH are two readings of the same solution, and at 25 °C they always sum to 14. A pOH of 4.5 is low, which means hydroxide is relatively plentiful, so the solution must be basic and its pH must be the complement, 9.5. A quick check: any pOH below 7 forces a pH above 7. That single relationship lets you convert between the two scales without recalculating concentrations.
source: OpenStax — Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e); NIST — Reference Data / Constants (https://www.nist.gov/pml)
